source: NASA/JPL Horizons API, queried 2026-10-19. Observer ephemeris of the Moon (301) from the Artemis II spacecraft (-1024) body center. Quantity 14 is the apparent sub-observer east longitude and latitude on the IAU MOON_ME body-fixed frame (Mean Earth / polar axis, east-longitude positive, +X at 0° east, +Y at 90° east, +Z north). Quantity 20 is the apparent range. Cartesian Moon-centered coordinates are range * (cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat), with range = delta_au * 149597870.700 km, the au printed in that Horizons header. This is not the BODY EQUATOR node-of-date vector frame, whose +X is the equator node and does not rotate with the Moon. https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api
query: COMMAND=301 MAKE_EPHEM=YES EPHEM_TYPE=OBSERVER CENTER=500@-1024 START_TIME='2026-04-06 18:00' STOP_TIME='2026-04-07 02:00' STEP_SIZE='1 m' QUANTITIES=14,20 ANG_FORMAT=DEG CSV_FORMAT=YES CAL_FORMAT=BOTH OBJ_DATA=NO
radiusNote: Center radii printed in the same Horizons header: 1737.4, 1737.4, 1737.4 km (Equator_a, b, pole_c). Target pole/equ: MOON_ME, east-longitude positive.
